newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent untraded, marked higher in late trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent untraded, marked higher in late trade.

text.p: September Brent futures were untraded but marked higher in late trading on Thursday as players moved to the sidelines to wait for direction from London, brokers said.
Weak markets in London and New York overnight prompted some caution in the market, brokers said.
The prospect of rapid Iraqi crude sales in August undermined both Brent and NYMEX overnight, outweighing sentiment over a tightening gasoline market in the United States.
Brokers said the Iraqi news had now been absorbed by the market.
By late trading on Thursday, September Brent was quoted at $18.33/$18.37 per barrel after London settled at $18.30.
NYMEX August crude was last traded at $19.64 per barrel on ACCESS, down one cent from London after trading a tight 14-cent range since the New York close.
One broker said he expected Brent to move sideways in the near term between $18.50 and $17.50.
Tom James of Credit Lyonnais Rouse said some technical support would be found around $18.25 -- a previous area of congestion.
